items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S8946

SPONSOR: LANZA
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the public authorities law, in
relation to enacting the "toll payer protection act"; and to repeal
certain provisions of such law relating thereto

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

This bill would enact a Toll Payers' Bill of Rights to improve the proc-
ess for notifying drivers about tolls and fines incurred; to ensure that
fines are fair; and that motor vehicle registrations are not suspended
because of an outstanding bill for a cashless toll fee.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1 of the bill establishes that this act shall be cited as "the
toll payer protection act."

Section 2 amends the article_9 of the public authorities law by adding a
new title 11-A, Cashless Tolls, to provide:

1. "Cashless tolling facility", "owner" and "notice of toll due" shall
have the meanings set forth, for purposes of this section.

2. A cashless toll notice shall be sent to an owner by first class mail
within thirty days of incurring such obligation.

3. The owner shall have thirty days from the date the notice of toll due
was sent by first class mail to pay the assessed toll.

4. The information that must be included in the notice.

5. If an owner fails to respond timely to the notice of toll due a
second notice shall be sent which may include a fee for late payment
which shall not exceed five dollars. The owner will have thirty days
after the second notice was sent to pay the toll and any fee.

6. If an owner fails to respond timely to the second notice of toll the
tolling facility may send a notice of liability and the owner shall have
ninety days from the date the notice of liability was sent to pay the
assessed toll or contest the notice.

7. If an owner fails to respond to the notice of liability or is found
liable for the assessed toll, the owner shall pay the assessed toll and
any fees which shall not exceed the amount of the toll and a monetary
penalty equal to twenty-five dollars or double the amount of the toll
due, whichever is greater.

8. Every public authority which operates a cashless tolling facility
shall promulgate rules and regulations that establish an installment
payment plan for the payment of any toll incurred and shall include this
information on the notice of toll due and the notice of liability and
display it conspicuously on the authorities' website.

9. Every public authority which operates a cashless tolling facility
shall establish a procedure to contest alleged liability or toll due
including a hearing and a right to appeal. This information shall be
included in the notice of toll due and the notice of liability.
10. Any toll fee that will be charged for usage of any bridge, tunnel,
road, or any other entity shall be displayed conspicuously and promi-
nently on signage to provide ample and adequate notice.

11. A prohibition of tolling authorities' ability to sell or transfer an
owner's debt to a debt collection agency unless one year has passed from
when the owner was found liable or the owner has a total debt owed to
the authority of one thousand dollars or more.

12. That no motor vehicle registration shall be suspended resulting from
an obligation to a pay a toll at a cashless tolling facility.

13. Every public authority which operates a cashless tolling facility
shall undertake a public awareness campaign regarding the use and proc-
ess for the payment of tolls; provide sufficient methods to obtain an
electronic device for the charging of tolls; and maintain a website and
toll-free number-for any person to receive updated information on any
tolls or fees which are outstanding, and where feasible, allow for the
receiving of such information by electronic mail or text message. Such
website and phone number shall be included on any notice of toll due or
notice of liability sent by the authority.

Section 3 Renumbers section 2985 to section 2985-b.

Section 4 Within 90 days of the effective date of this act, requires the
Triborough bridge and tunnel authority to implement an amnesty program
for any person who owes tolls, fines, fees or penalties for a toll
incurred at any cashless tolling facility operated by the authority for
a period of at least five weeks for toll obligations incurred on or
after November 1, 2016.

Section 5 is the effective date.

 
DIFFERENCE BETWEEN ORIGINAL AND AMENDED VERSION:

The amended bill amends the public authorities law; provides that a
motor vehicle registration may not be suspended due to an obligation to
pay a cashless toll; limits the amount of penalties for unpaid obli-
gations; establishes a process -for the transfer of debt owed to the
public authority to a debt collection agency; and requires the implemen-
tation of an amnesty program for cashless tolls and penalties incurred
at any cashless tolling facility operated by the Triborough Bridge and
Tunnel Authority.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Over the last few years, New York State has been implementing a system
of cashless tolling (EZPass) on its bridges, tunnels and roadways.
While such a system has many benefits, including decreasing traffic
congestion and increasing efficiency, many serious problems have arisen.

The cashless toll system has caused confusion among many drivers.

Notice of toll fees mailed (Tolls by Mail) to drivers without EZPass
often take several weeks to arrive, and in many instances, are not
received at all. All too often owners who do not receive the Tolls by
Mail notice of fees end up incurring significant late fees and fines.
In addition, the instances of inconsistent or unexplained fees have also
occurred. Even more concerning, some owners have had their car registra-
tions suspended, been stopped on the road, had their cars seized and
have been left stranded due to alleged unpaid Tolls by Mail fees.

This Toll Payers' Protection Act would help alleviate these problems and
lessen unnecessary and excessive late fees by establishing a clear and
fair process of notification of Tolls by Mail.

Additionally, this bill would establish appropriate penalties for
nonpayment of toll fees and protect owners by preventing the suspension
of car registrations due to alleged unpaid fees.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

None

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the one hundred and twentieth day after it
shall have become a law. Effective immediately, any authority or agency
shall take any actions necessary to adopt, amend or repeal regulations
in order to implement the provisions of this act by such effective date.

summary: Enacts the "toll payer protection act" to establish a New York toll payers' bill of rights; provides that any person, firm, corporation, or other entity who is charged with the payment of a cashless toll fee in the state of New York shall have the option to be notified by text message or electronic mail that such fee has been so charged, the entity to which such fee must be paid, and the date by when such fee must be paid; further provides for the establishment of a payment plan for the payment of a toll fee and any related penalties; makes related provisions.
